name: strawberry compote
instructions:
1. Sauté strawberries in lemon juice — 1/4 of a lemon is enough. Don't overdo the lemon in the early stages (see notes — easy failure mode).
2. Add sugar. Cook and stir/crush rapidly until syrupy.
3. Mix 1-2 tablespoons of water with cornstarch and stir in for desired thickness. Hard to under- or over-do.

Blueberries can go in alongside the strawberries. Vanilla and salt also go in.
notes:
=== LEMON JUICE — GO EASY AT THE START ===

1/4 of a lemon is enough. The strawberries will add their own tartness as they cook, so don't overdo the lemon in the early stages — easy failure mode.

=== CORNSTARCH SLURRY FOR THICKNESS ===

1-2 tablespoons of water mixed with cornstarch, stirred in. Hard to under- or over-do — adjust to the thickness you want.

=== NOT SHELF-STABLE — NEEDS REFRIGERATION ===

Compote is not shelf-stable — keep it refrigerated. Same non-shelf-stable class as cream-cheese-frosting. In the cake-topping family, the shelf-stable picks are buttercream-frosting and bakers-frosting; chocolate-ganache sits in between.

=== SIBLING RECIPE ===

Chia jam (chia-jam.json) — different thickening mechanism (chia seeds instead of cornstarch), different final texture. Reach for whichever fits.
